text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Garnett
text_blocks.text: Everybody has a profile. If you were going to play Shaq, you probably want to play him the same way you would play Dwight Howard. I wouldn't dare try to back Shaq down. Shaq's bigger than me. I would what I call face him. I would use more guard skills against Shaq, getting him to move laterally, and that's how it's going with Shaq.

text_blocks.speaker: N3on
text_blocks.text: So you would never go in?

text_blocks.text: No, that's the game I wouldn't win. He's bigger, he wins that. When we face up, we have to play like we have to play guard. I'll win that. I'm quicker and faster. Every time.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Garnett
quotes.summary_phrase: Kevin Garnett breaks down Stephen Curry's shooting mechanics
quotes.excerpt: The first tip on Stephen Curry is that he always gets what we call his eyes up.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Garnett
text_blocks.text: The first tip on Stephen Curry is that he always gets what we call his eyes up. Do you understand that? Eyes on the rim. That's the problem, I always look down. So listen to me. It don't matter what move you do. You can do this, you can do this. When you go to shoot, the first thing got to come up is your eyes. You got to locate. You can't be doing this and then your eyes be the last thing to locate.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Garnett
text_blocks.text: So we use this as a pump fake. So you see Stephen Curry hold the ball. You ever see Stephen Curry go? Yeah. It's a pump fake. And that's called eyes up, because when he looks up, you think he's going to shoot, and then he hezzy. Then he goes down, he goes boom boom, he looks up, you go, you go. So use this every time you look up, like a jump shot or like a pump fake.

text_blocks.text: So before, when you started this, it was more of trying to bring in people to view you doing certain things and then that's why all this outlandish stuff came from?

It was when I was a kid and I wasn't thinking and it was it was real it was a really, really bad mindset.
